hub_subtitle: From hesitant communicator to confident global business leader

lesson.menu_desc: Not every important meeting is about business. In Milton's building in the US, the owners are paying a special assessment, the pool has been closed since May, and tonight there is an election. Linda, the board president, wants to nominate him. Learn mixed conditionals to connect past decisions with today's results (if the board had hired a better contractor, the pool would be open today) and the language of a condo association: bylaws, quorum, proxy, nominate, ballot, amenity, contractor, reserve fund — 35 slides

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: To officially suggest a person for a position or an election
The paper or list that people use to vote in an election
The minimum number of people needed for a meeting to make official decisions
The official rules that an association or building must follow
A person or company paid to do a specific job, like a repair
Money a building saves for big repairs in the future
A document that lets another person vote for you
Something in a building that makes life easier or more pleasant, like a pool or a gym

items.situation: You can't go to the meeting on Tuesday. Tell Linda what you will do.
The pool is closed because the board chose a bad contractor. Say it in one sentence.
Ask the president if the meeting can start.
You did not read the rules, and now you do not understand the vote. Say it.
Politely ask to speak at the meeting.
Tell the owners you accept the nomination.

listenings.text: Good evening, everyone. This is Patricia Lowe, your property manager, with a short update before Tuesday's annual meeting. First, the roof. As you know, the repair cost two hundred thousand dollars. If the building had saved more in past years, the reserve fund would be healthy today, and nobody would be paying a special assessment. The new board will have to fix that. Second, the pool. We have received bids from three new contractors. The cheapest one can start in November. I know it's frustrating. If we had chosen a contractor with better references last spring, the pool would be open right now. Third, the election. Two seats are open on the board, and owners can be nominated at the meeting. And please, if you can't come, sign a proxy. Last year we didn't have a quorum, and that's why the bylaws are still not updated. See you on Tuesday at seven, in the lobby lounge.

Hi, I'm Tom. Three years ago I joined the board of my building, and I made almost every mistake a new member can make. My first mistake was simple: I didn't read the bylaws. If I had read them, I would have known that the board can't spend more than fifty thousand dollars without a vote of the owners. I approved a new gym, and we had to cancel the contract. My second mistake was trying to do everything alone. Today I'm a better board member, because I ask questions before I vote. If I were starting today, I would do three things. I'd read the bylaws in the first week. I'd meet the property manager before the first meeting. And I'd talk to the owners who never come, because they're the people who send a proxy and then complain. Being on a board isn't a title. It's a job, and nobody pays you to do it. But if more good people ran for their boards, our buildings would be much better places to live.
